newsitem.title: UK: UK government takes some moves to free up casinos.
newsitem.headline: UK government takes some moves to free up casinos.

text.p: The government said on Tuesday it would ask parliament to approve a series of measures to free British casinos from restrictions which make them some of the most tightly regulated gaming houses in the world.
But a spokeswoman for the Home Office (interior ministry) said the government was still considering whether to implement other suggestions made in a consultation document in February.

Home Office Minister Timothy Kirkhope said in a written parliamentary answer that he would ask MPs to allow casino bars to stay open until 0200 hours in the provinces and 0300 hours in London, instead of shutting before midnight along with pubs.
Kirkhope also said he proposed to alter the rule under which punters must apply for membership of a casino in advance.

At present, a gambler must wait 48 hours between visiting a casino to make a membership application and being allowed to play at the tables. Kirkhope wants the period to be cut to 24 hours, making membership easier for short-term visitors.
Kirkhope said he would also propose that debit cards -- though not credit cards -- should be allowed in casinos.
But the spokeswoman said proposals in the consultation document to allow casinos in 13 more British towns were still being considered.

She said there would be further consultation on plans for a major increase in the number of slot machines casinos could have, and proposals to allow them limited rights to advertise their facilities, and to permit postal applications for membership.

Kirkhope also said he would propose to parliament later this year a removal of restrictions on print advertising by bingo clubs, and might even suggest they should be able to advertise on the broadcast media. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
